objective.name: pilot.launch
objective.description: Launches a pilot: creates a continuity associated with a Matter or Capacity pilot, optionally attached to a parent, and hands it its first message, which starts the pilot. When a parent launches it with a task, the answer is the result of the pilot.

#root.role: Create one continuity associated with a pilot (a Matter pilot_definition or a Capacity), optionally attached to a parent, and hand it its first message so that the pilot starts. When a parent launches a task, wait for the pilot to finish treating it and answer with its result, as any capacity answers the intention that called it.

parent_id._comment: Optional. The continuity that launches; absent for a root.

message._comment: Optional. The first message: { content, id? }. Absent, the continuity waits for its first message.

wait._comment: Optional. Wait for the pilot to finish treating the first message and answer with its result. Default: true when parent_id and message are both given (a parent delegating a task), false otherwise (an interface opening a chat must not wait).

seq._comment: Line of the first message in the journal; null without a message.

result._comment: Only when the call waited. { text, messages: [{ to, kind, content }] }: what the pilot said, in order, while treating the first message. text is the contents joined by blank lines.

treated._comment: True when the call waited and the pilot finished the first message.

effects.continuity: Creates the continuity (journal, header, mailbox, runtime) through continuity.create and attaches it to its parent when there is one.
effects.mailbox: Hands the first message to the continuity through mailbox.send.
effects.external: The first message wakes the pilot of the new continuity, asynchronously. With wait, pilot.launch then waits for the pilot to finish the message, acknowledging itself as long-running (a running response every few seconds) and giving back its execution slot while it waits.

transformation_contract.morphing: A pilot reference, a founding intention and an optional first message become a new continuity whose pilot has started on that message; when the call waits, the answer is what the pilot said while treating it.
invariants: The continuity is created by continuity.create from the pilot_ref, the founding intention and the parent_id given; a Matter pilot and a Capacity pilot are launched the same way.
The first message, when given, is of kind user; its sender is continuity:<parent_id> when there is a parent and user:1 for a root; its identifier is the one given or <continuity_id>_launch.
Without a message the continuity is created and waits for its first message.
Every step is idempotent: the same call again creates nothing twice and sends nothing twice.
The same continuity_id with another pilot, intention or parent is an identity conflict, refused.
No message is sent when the creation failed.
pilot.launch writes no Matter itself: every mutation goes through the capacities it composes.
The first message is handed over by mailbox.send, which wakes the pilot: pilot.launch never activates the pilot explicitly.

Without wait the answer comes at once and carries no result of the pilot; with wait the answer is given when the pilot has finished the first message and is at rest: its continuity is idle, its mailbox is empty, no wait group is active and no awaited intention is still without its Response, and it stays so for a short moment (LAUNCH_SETTLE_S); acknowledging the first message is not enough, since a pilot that emits an awaited intention without a wait group ends its turn and goes on with new messages.
wait defaults to true only when both parent_id and message are given; a root launch (an interface opening a chat) answers at once.

The result is read from the journal of the launched continuity, never from a field the model must aim at: the messages of kind pilot written after the first message, whoever they are addressed to, in order. A pilot that said nothing gives an empty result.
The wait follows a succession: if the continuity is replaced by its successor while treating the message, the successor's treatment is awaited and its messages are part of the result.

While it waits the call acknowledges itself as running at regular intervals and yields its execution slot; it is bounded (setting LAUNCH_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S) and a bound reached is a refusal, not a silent stop.

A message the pilot could not treat (set aside after its attempts), the first one or a later one of the same task, is an error answer, not a result, and it carries the cause: the error of the last failed attempt.
success: The continuity exists, attached to its parent, and its first message is accepted in its journal.
failure: Fails with an invalid request when continuity_id, pilot_ref or initial_intention is missing, or when message has no content.
Fails when the pilot named by pilot_ref or the parent named by parent_id does not exist, before any message is sent.
Fails refused (reason message_parked) when the pilot could not treat the first message and set it aside; refused (reason timeout) when the wait bound is reached; invalid when wait is not a boolean.
notes: The policy of the pilot that asks for a launch is applied by pilot.activate to the pilot_ref, before any effect.

#create.role: Create the continuity with its pilot, its founding intention and its parent.

transformation_contract.morphing: A pilot reference and a founding intention become an idle continuity.

#hand_over.role: Hand the first message to the continuity, which wakes its pilot.

transformation_contract.morphing: A task becomes the first message of the continuity.

#await_result.role: When waiting, wait for the pilot to finish the first message and read what it said.

transformation_contract.morphing: The rest of the continuity (or of its successor) after the task becomes the result: the messages of kind pilot written since the first message.
